input.question: What is it about teeth in that when they break flesh when biting, they make the subject so susceptable to any disease the owner of said chomps has?
input.ground_truth: Nothing. You have this backwards. If you puncture skin and flesh with **anything** that has bacteria on it, that bacteria now gets in the wound. Teeth, a sharp stick, a rock, glass, metal, whatever. Step on a rusty nail, and see how quickly they treat you for the bacteria that *might* have been on it. Teeth may stand out because, in many cases, they're *designed* to break skin and tear flesh, and this is done by animals that don't tend to have fantastic oral hygiene.

Question: What is it about teeth in that when they break flesh when biting, they make the subject so susceptable to any disease the owner of said chomps has?

response.prediction: Okay! Imagine your mouth has tiny doors called teeth. When those doors (teeth) bite into something soft like skin, they can make a little cut or hole. Germs that live in the mouth can sneak through those tiny holes into the body. Once the germs get inside, they can make you sick because your body doesn’t like those germs. So, if someone bites you and their mouth has germs, those germs can go into your body and make you sick. That’s why it’s not safe to let someone bite you!
